historical_context.time_period: Existential Collapse era, during the 2779 Internal Serenity Review
historical_context.location: Stillwater Six, a Framgång alignment clinic in an Enceladus ring-pilgrimage transfer habitat.
historical_context.summary: A hospitality worker subjected to a mandatory alignment session must decide whether to expose her protected neural stream, prove the clinic lead's false disposition through separately owned nonclinical records, make the order public, or distribute evidence through quiet worker custody.

public_facts.text: Framgång sold therapeutic alignment services to individuals, employers, and insurers, and maintained its strongest territorial presence around Enceladus and Saturn's ring-linked pilgrimage routes.
NeuroSyn systems measured affect, attention, safety, and compliance while providing useful workplace and clinical interface functions.
The Internal Serenity Review found therapeutic affect shaping, compliance architecture, and coercive reward loops technically inseparable in some flagship products.
The Review redistributed openly coercive work into harder markets rather than abolishing the underlying systems.

ambient_pressures.text: Protected-session privacy keeps employer-funded care usable but allows clinic management to publish a clean administrative shell around coercive interface events.
Workers' employment, debt, care eligibility, shifts, and technical credentials make disclosure materially costly even when no single authority can lawfully inspect all relevant records.
A disclosure can preserve patient privacy by joining a supervisor route order with hardware maintenance events; neither surface contains the patient's thoughts.

groups.label: Stillwater Six hospitality and reset workers
institutional_logic: Keep rooms, guests, and clinic routines functioning while remaining eligible for wages, housing-linked debt terms, and employer-funded care.
material_incentives: Preserve evidence without making one patient carry it alone
internal_virtues: Not demanding another worker's private account
internal_shames: Turning a coworker into a public exhibit
Leaving one worker as the only witness
Mistaking a clean room for a harmless clinic
prestige_markers: A rota covered without surrendering leverage
A receipt kept past routine collection
Knowing which imperfection another worker will read
taboo_triggers: Therapeutic language used to erase ordered labor
Being asked to perform calm for customers
emotional_display_norms: Fear and care travel through task-sharing, jokes, carried objects, and quiet corrections more safely than through formal declarations.
trust_defaults: Trusts coworkers in bounded tasks; distrusts records owned entirely by clinic management; protects patient-specific content unless the patient chooses otherwise.
speech_register_cues: Concrete descriptions of who ordered what

groups.label: Framgång clinic management
institutional_logic: Sell useful care, preserve the privacy promise, produce comparable dispositions, and keep employer clients from seeing coercion as liability.
internal_shames: Conflicting records joined outside clinic custody
taboo_triggers: Asking whether voluntary care was ordered
emotional_display_norms: Concern must remain polished; anger is translated into patient safety, privacy, or staff fitness language.
trust_defaults: Trusts signed dispositions, clinical custody, and customer-facing calm; treats worker-held receipts as contaminated context.

groups.label: NeuroSyn interface maintenance contractors
institutional_logic: Keep clinical interfaces within safety and compatibility tolerances while remaining outside clinical interpretation authority.
internal_virtues: A maintenance exception used only when a machine state requires it
internal_shames: Letting management turn a hardware event into a therapeutic opinion
prestige_markers: A service record that survives vendor dispute
taboo_triggers: Being told a safety interlock is merely emotional
Clinical managers claiming ownership of maintenance facts
emotional_display_norms: Alarm is compressed into dry diagnosis and equipment jokes.
trust_defaults: Trusts device counters within their narrow scope; does not treat counters as proof of motive or subjective state.

groups.label: PSC insurer auditors
institutional_logic: Make incompatible corporate records comparable enough to price risk without assuming authority over every underlying system.
material_incentives: Keep insurers from inheriting undisclosed coercion
internal_shames: Accepting one institution's summary as the whole event
prestige_markers: A finding that survives cross-jurisdiction challenge
A contradiction proved without excess disclosure
taboo_triggers: An insurer paying for risk hidden behind incomparable categories
emotional_display_norms: Concern appears as exact scope, repeated wording, sealed objects, and refusal to infer beyond the evidence.
trust_defaults: Trusts separately owned records more when their contradiction survives without one owner interpreting all of them.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: Workers need evidence strong enough to survive management while refusing to make a coworker's exposed mind the price of being believed.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Offer actions that share shifts, split receipts, hold narrow witness, and preserve patient choice instead of defaulting to total disclosure.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: Clinic management treats a real privacy boundary as proof that its own signed disposition should remain the only readable account.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Management dialogue should defend custody and clean summaries without claiming the privacy rule itself is fake.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: The auditor gains legitimate leverage by joining narrow records, not by demanding a patient's complete neural stream.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Keep Kira's actions inside consent, sealing, comparison, and exact questions; she is an auditor, not a rescuer or mind reader.

target_self_read: Workers ordered into unpaid treatment after refusing dangerous scheduling
Witnesses holding different parts of the same event
misread_patterns: Treats shared evidence custody as contagion or gossip
factional_misread_matrix.projection_use: Let Sel sincerely value care while using its language to erase the employment order and the interface escalation.

target_self_read: People whose jobs, care, rest, and housing pressure are part of the event
misread_patterns: May value a worker only when the worker becomes admissible evidence
May preserve privacy while ignoring retaliation after the finding
factional_misread_matrix.projection_use: Keep Kira useful and bounded; her finding can expose a contradiction without repairing Esi's rota, debt, or employment.

observer_read: Possible witnesses who can still retreat into technical neutrality
target_self_read: Credentialed technicians authorized to describe hardware events, not clinical meaning
misread_patterns: Workers may expect a counter to prove coercion by itself
Technicians may understate how their silence protects a false disposition
factional_misread_matrix.projection_use: Jon must state what the counter proves and what it cannot prove, then choose whether his credential becomes part of the evidence.

role_pressure_fields.summary: A low-status clinic worker whose body and route order carry knowledge that the audit shell excludes.
obligations: Avoid making coworkers responsible for her mind
available_masks: Cleaning movement that looks beneath notice
failure_modes: Letting management archive the only route receipt

role_pressure_fields.summary: A credentialed technician who can preserve hardware events while lacking authority over clinical interpretation or patient content.
obligations: Stay inside consent and technical scope
failure_modes: Letting purge erase the only independent event record
Turning helpful access into control over Esi's choice

role_pressure_fields.summary: A clinician-manager whose care authority, contract performance, and audit exposure converge in one signed disposition.
failure_modes: A separately owned record contradicts the disposition
A public waiting room becomes a witness
Privacy is separated from management custody

role_pressure_fields.summary: A bounded auditor who can seal nonclinical evidence and request a patient-limited hold but cannot cross the privacy line on her own authority.

known_context.text: Esi knows she was ordered into Room C after refusing a double shift, remembers the reward-shaped loss of importance around her refusal, and can read her own route receipt.

beliefs.text: Esi believes privacy matters and that being believed should not automatically require giving an institution her complete session stream.

misreads.text: Esi may overestimate what one receipt or one public statement can force an insurer to do.

must_not_know.text: Esi must not know the full Review pattern beyond Stillwater Six before Kira joins or compares records.

known_context.text: Jon knows the maintenance counter recorded four reward pulses, one interlock, and a scheduled purge; he cannot see session content or infer the patient's exact subjective experience.

beliefs.text: Jon believes a hardware event should remain a hardware fact even when management has a cleaner clinical interpretation.

misreads.text: Jon may treat credential loss as the main cost because technical labor is the pressure he understands most directly.

must_not_know.text: Jon must not narrate Esi's thoughts, refusal details, or clinical state beyond what she tells or visibly shows him.

known_context.text: Kira knows her audit authority, the shell fields, the privacy exclusion, and how to seal separately owned records.

beliefs.text: Kira believes contradictions among narrow records can justify comparison without treating broad access as care.

misreads.text: Kira may underestimate retaliation that arrives as rota, credential, care, or debt administration after she leaves.

must_not_know.text: Kira must not know the session stream, supervisor order, or counter values until Esi, Jon, or a sealed record makes them available.

known_context.text: Sel knows he ordered and operated the session, signed the clean disposition, and can invoke protected-session custody and routine purge policy.

beliefs.text: Sel treats returning a worker to duty and preserving clinic legitimacy as compatible with care.

misreads.text: Sel reads distributed worker custody as contamination because no single authorized professional controls the joined story.

must_not_know.text: Sel must not know which evidence workers have retained until their observable actions reveal it.

author_only_boundaries.text: The Review will contribute to the NeuroPulse spinout, but no Stillwater Six participant should speak as if the future administrative split is already settled.

The later Enceladus Cooperative Schism confirms persistent worker-pilgrim pressure in Framgång's Saturn economy; this 2779 fixture may show mutual aid but not a mature cooperative movement at Stillwater Six.

A cooperative neural-repair clinic can receive narrowly consented records through Free Neural Network practice, but it does not gain authority over Esi's clinical content or turn the scene into movement recruitment.
